sources.title: MiniMax M2.5: Built for Real-World Productivity
sources.evidence: Dated 2026-02-12. Announces M2.5 and M2.5-Lightning together as equal-capability versions with different serving speed; describes reasoning, coding and tool use.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5 product page
sources.evidence: M2.5-specific body names M2.5 and M2.5-highspeed as the two API versions with identical results, and links the M2.5 Hugging Face weights. Current navigation names M3; the M2.5 body is legacy product evidence, not proof of present API availability.

sources.title: Will M2.5-Lightning be released?
sources.evidence: MiniMax org reply on February 13 says Lightning uses more inference resources for speed while model parameters remain exactly the same. Together with the official two-version product descriptions, this supports shared M2.5 weights for highspeed.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5 model-size discussion
sources.evidence: February 15 official-org reply says all M2-series models have 230B parameters and points to an M2.5 quantization. The 10B-active wording is in a community member title, not in the official reply.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 configuration
sources.evidence: Defines MiniMaxM2ForCausalLM: 62 layers, 3072 hidden size, 256 local experts and top-8 routing, 48 query/8 KV heads, 128 head dimension, 196608 maximum positions, and FP8 block quantization.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 reference implementation
sources.evidence: Implements decoder-only attention plus routed MoE; e_score_correction_bias is registered as a buffer. Token embedding and output weights are untied. No MTP module is constructed by this reference implementation.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 checkpoint index and shard headers
sources.evidence: All 96103 indexed keys were matched to bounded shard headers cached by audit303 and independently recounted here. There are 228689748992 reference-registered weight elements, 15872 routing-bias values and 13880064 FP8 scale entries. Buffer registration does not establish whether the routing values were originally learned. No MTP keys occur.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 Model License
sources.evidence: Named MiniMax Model License grants use, modification and redistribution subject to attribution, agreement and prohibited-use requirements. Header gives weights-version release date 2026-02-13; the card labels the license modified-mit.

sources.title: MiniMax OpenAI SDK compatibility
sources.evidence: Exact MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed ID remains in the multi-turn tool-call reasoning note, which requires preserving think content. Current supported-model/context table contains only M3 variants; it does not establish the former highspeed API limit.

sources.title: MiniMax Anthropic SDK compatibility
sources.evidence: States M2.5-series inputs are text and tool-call content, without image/video input, and M2.x thinking cannot be disabled. Current endpoint support table lists M3 variants only.

sources.title: MiniMax model release notes
sources.evidence: February 2026 entry explicitly names the MiniMax-M2.5/M2.5-highspeed series release. Does not provide a release day.

sources.title: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence
sources.evidence: May 2026 first-party report covers evolution through M2.5/M2.7 but its explicit 229.9B total and 9.8B active architecture statement labels M2. These values are not directly assigned to M2.5-highspeed.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 model card and weights
sources.evidence: Official downloadable text-generation checkpoint, modified-mit card metadata, local serving instructions and tool-calling guide. Its automatic parameter counter is not a learned-weight count.

sources.title: Frozen Models.dev source lead
sources.evidence: Frozen catalog supplied 204800 API context and February 13 date. This lead is not independent primary verification.

sources.title: MiniMax retired model list
sources.evidence: FAQ table labels M2.5/highspeed retired. The notice separately says new-user access ends October 19 and final pay-as-you-go retirement is November 18, 2026; M Plan/Token Plan requests have been rerouted since October 19. These conflicting lifecycle presentations do not prove current endpoint operation.

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway MiniMax M2.5 highspeed provider metadata
sources.evidence: Exact primaryModel minimax-m2.5-highspeed with provider minimax has contextSize 204800 in embedded page data; rendered provider row rounds it to 205K. This establishes the advertised Vercel-to-MiniMax route limit, not independent native endpoint operation.

name.note: Exact API identifier. The launch called the fast serving version M2.5-Lightning; the matching two-version descriptions establish the alias relationship.

family.note: Retains the catalog family key; specifically part of MiniMax M2-series/M2.5.

release_date.note: Earliest public launch of the fast version alongside M2.5. February 13 in the weights license is a later checkpoint-version date, not the earliest API announcement.

open_weights.note: Highspeed is a serving mode of the released M2.5 model. The official product page links the shared weights and the org reply rules out a separate Lightning parameter set.

license.note: Actual distributed license title. Model-card metadata still labels it modified-mit, but the distributed agreement contains its own notice and prohibited-use terms; this is not plain MIT. Hosted API terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Developer nominal 230B. Shared released checkpoint has 228.689764864B non-scale elements, including 15872 routing-bias values whose original training status is unresolved for M2.5. The reference registers 228.689748992B parameter elements. Neither storage subtotal is promoted to an exact learned count; M2-specific 229.9B is not transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact-variant developer scalar with a clear counting convention was found. Top-8 routing yields 9.801344B active non-embedding weights; counting complete embedding/output matrices gives 11.030537216B. The report explicitly assigns 9.8B to M2. These are explicitly scoped derivations, not a developer-disclosed activated count.

architecture.note: Decoder-only Transformer with full grouped-query attention and routed MoE; 62 layers, 256 experts, eight selected per token. Lightning is a serving name and does not establish Lightning Attention.

context_window.note: Exact Vercel gateway metadata advertises 204800 for the MiniMax-backed highspeed route. Shared checkpoint native max_position_embeddings is 196608. Current native API tables removed this model, so this is a provider-specific hosted limit, not a fresh native-endpoint verification.

modalities.note: Text language model; MiniMax explicitly excludes image/video input for M2.5-series. Tool-call serialization does not add a sensory modality.

reasoning.note: Exact highspeed API note preserves think output; M2.x thinking is always enabled.

tool_call.note: Exact highspeed API note documents tool-call conversation handling, reinforced by release notes and shared-weight tool guide.

description.value: Faster serving version of MiniMax M2.5 for text reasoning, coding and tool-using agents, using the same underlying model parameters.
description.note: Replaces generic latency wording with the verified serving-mode relationship and supported capabilities.

patch.description: Faster serving version of MiniMax M2.5 for text reasoning, coding and tool-using agents, using the same underlying model parameters.
patch.notes: Highspeed/Lightning is the faster serving mode of M2.5 with unchanged parameters. 230B is the developer nominal count. Shared checkpoint has 228.689764864B non-scale elements including 15872 routing-bias values whose original training status remains unresolved. Active count is unverified; scoped derivations differ with embedding conventions. Vercel gateway metadata advertises a 204800-token MiniMax-backed highspeed route; shared checkpoint max_position_embeddings is 196608. Native API tables removed the model. The FAQ labels it retired but also gives November 18 final pay-as-you-go retirement and October 19 access restrictions/plan rerouting. Shared downloadable weights use the MiniMax Model License; card metadata labels it modified-mit.

summary: Verified the shared-weight highspeed/Lightning relationship, nominal 230B, MoE, custom MiniMax Model License, native reasoning/tools and February 12 launch. Exact activated count remains unverified. Provider-specific Vercel metadata verifies 204800 hosted context, separately from the 196608 checkpoint limit. Checkpoint storage and reference-registered parameter subtotals are qualified because routing-bias training status is unresolved.
